text: {"standards":[{"code":"L.6.4.b","verdict":"partly","reason":"Part B has students use the Greek roots mythos and logy to decode mythology and extend to geology and zoology, but the affix/root work is teacher-led explanation rather than students independently using roots to determine an unknown word's meaning."},{"code":"RI.6.1","verdict":"taught","reason":"Part A's annotation of the three unlabeled Prometheus/Pandora passages has students underline evidence and pair it with inferences about problem, world, and values, and the Quick Write asks for a clue supporting their thinking."},{"code":"RI.6.4","verdict":"partly","reason":"Part A has students infer word meaning from context (the 'chained' example) and the extension asks about connotation, but most of the lesson's word-meaning work is teacher-modeled and the connotation prompt is only an optional extension."},{"code":"SL.6.1.a","verdict":"taught","reason":"The Think-Pair-Share in Whole-Class Initial Ideas and the Part B huddle require students to cite their annotated text evidence and build on peers' ideas during discussion."}],"anchorText":{"verdict":"uses","reason":"The Launch reads the full 'What Are Myths?' article and Part A uses three unlabeled Coolidge Prometheus/Pandora passages, matching both listed texts, though the lesson does not specify page numbers."}}
